grammar.title: 2A: Present perfect and past simple
grammar.explanation:
Use the **present perfect** (**have/has** + past participle) for life experiences when you do not say when. Example idea: I have visited the market many times.

Use the **present perfect** for recent past actions with a result now. I have just bought fruit at the market, and now I have the fruit at home.

Use **never**, **ever**, **yet**, **already**, and **just** with the **present perfect**. Have you ever met my neighbor?

Use the **past simple** for finished actions when we say, ask, or know when they happened. I visited the cinema last night.

Never use the **present perfect** with a past time word like **yesterday**, **last week**, or **last night**.
examples: I *have visited* the market many times. (present perfect - no time given)
She *has lived* in this apartment for two years. (present perfect - still true now)
They *have just left* the cinema. (present perfect - recent, result now)
Have you *ever* been to a quiet park? (present perfect - life experience)
I *haven't seen* my neighbor yet. (present perfect - not finished)
We *visited* the hospital yesterday. (past simple - we know when)
She *bought* fruit at the market last Sunday. (past simple - past time word)
I *went* to the cinema last night. (past simple - last night)
A big crowd *waited* outside the cinema. (past simple - finished action)
We *walked* down the street this morning. (past simple - finished time)

practice.q: Complete the sentence: I ___ (visit) the park many times.
practice.a: I have visited the park many times.

practice.q: Correct the mistake: I have visited the cinema yesterday.
practice.a: I visited the cinema yesterday. Use the past simple with 'yesterday'.

practice.q: Which is correct: 'She has never met my neighbor' or 'She never has met my neighbor'?
practice.a: She has never met my neighbor. 'Never' goes before the main verb.
